proposal.name: Grouped singleton rotary embeddings
proposal.idea: Apply each layer’s original RoPE to all speculative positions using a batch of singleton sequences with explicit per-position offsets. Consume the existing contiguous projection blocks directly, then expose singleton queries and transposed KV views to the unchanged attention and cache paths.
proposal.cost_removed: For m verification positions across 30 layers, reduce RoPE calls from 60m to 60: 1,020 become 60 at m=17. Replace the 60 explicit key/value concatenations with views, removing 391,680 bytes of concatenation payload at m=17. These are operation and payload counts, not measured memory traffic. Dense projection and attention work remain unchanged.
proposal.source_evidence: candidate/inference.py:273–300 already produces contiguous Q/K/V blocks, splits them into positions, invokes singleton Q and K RoPE for every position, and concatenates keys and values again. The pinned MLX API supports a vector of offsets, one per batch element. [RoPE API](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.fast.rope.html). Its scalar and general implementations use matching frequency, angle, rotation, and output-conversion expressions. With sequence length one and offset[i]=C+i, their position arguments coincide without changing any reduction. [RoPE implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/rope.metal). An in-memory address audit passed 86,400 pair/view mapping checks across m=3 through 17; this does not establish native numerical parity.
proposal.generalization: Batching independent rotary operations and removing intermediate packing reduces invocation, allocation, and copying work without custom kernels or compiler changes. It can help deep or tensor-parallel speculative verifiers that preserve singleton arithmetic. Other backends require numerical audits; engines already batching RoPE gain nothing further, and benefits diminish when weight or attention traffic dominates.
proposal.risk: Scalar and batched RoPE use different native entrypoints, so matching source expressions still require bitwise validation. Incorrect batch/head mapping or offsets would corrupt retained keys. Strided KV insertion may introduce internal copies, and remaining dense work may outweigh the invocation savings.
proposal.history_relation: Builds on rounds 0013, 0016, and 0017, which provide bulk KV insertion and contiguous activation blocks while deliberately retaining singleton RoPE. Round 0001’s full-transformer numerical failure did not isolate rotary operations. This experiment retains the accepted projections and singleton attention; it does not repeat round 0005’s weight packing or the rejected drafting and vocabulary-screening policies.

research.plan:
1. Modify only candidate/. Enable the rotary grouping within the existing eligible grouped verifier, for m=3 through 17, native BF16 tensors, full 64-dimensional native RoPE, and offsets representable as signed 32-bit integers. Decide eligibility before cache mutation. Preserve the current rotary path for unsupported cases without disabling accepted projection grouping.

2. Create one int32 offsets vector [C,...,C+m-1] during decode and reuse it across layers. After the existing Q/K/V projection barriers, reshape Q and K blocks to [m,9,1,64] and [m,3,1,64]. Invoke the original attn.rope once on each, passing the vector offsets and retaining every module parameter and dtype.

3. Split rotated Q along batch into contiguous [1,9,1,64] singleton views. Transpose rotated K with axes (2,1,0,3) to [1,3,m,64]. Reshape V to [m,3,1,64] and apply the same transpose. Pass these views directly to the existing single bulk KV update, eliminating the two concatenations. Preserve functional buffer ownership and completion dependencies.

4. Keep sequential singleton attention against the original allocated-buffer prefixes ending at C+i+1, followed by the unchanged projections, heads, acceptance, and rollback. Preserve scalar pipelining, prefill, output budgets, shared model objects, and request isolation. Charge all offset construction and generated-token work to decode.

5. Extend candidate/checks.py with bitwise comparisons against the previous verifier and actual singleton reference calls. Cover every block length, both head counts, varied offsets, cancellation and BF16 rounding cases, rotated tensors, downstream logits, and retained KV. Update candidate RoPE hooks for vector offsets while keeping the scalar oracle independent. Exercise every acceptance boundary, stale-tail overwrite, capacity boundaries, scalar continuation, and fallback. Resolve the first numerical discrepancy before activation.

6. Add request-local counters showing two rotary calls per layer on active blocks. Freeze the implementation independently of benchmark prompts and results. Hand authoritative exact-token evaluation and benchmarking against the current best to the orchestrator; retain only an incremental gain of at least 1.03x in both confirmations.
research.reason: The current contiguous verifier exposes a substantial, untested reduction in repeated operations with a concrete arithmetic-equivalence argument. Native parity and net throughput remain uncertain enough to warrant evaluation and benchmarking.

proposal.name: Grouped singleton rotary embeddings
proposal.idea: Apply each layer’s unchanged RoPE to speculative positions as a batch of singleton sequences with explicit per-position offsets. Consume the existing contiguous projection blocks, then expose singleton queries and transposed KV views to the existing attention and cache paths.
proposal.cost_removed: For m verification positions across 30 layers, reduce RoPE calls from 60m to 60: 1,020 become 60 at m=17. Remove 60 explicit KV concatenations and their 391,680-byte BF16 output payload at m=17. These are operation and payload counts, not measured memory traffic. Cache insertion, dense projections, attention, offset construction, and views still cost work.
proposal.source_evidence: Verified the projection blocks, singleton rotary calls, and KV concatenations in [candidate/inference.py](candidate/inference.py:273), installed MLX 0.32.3, and the pinned checkpoint’s native 64-dimensional RoPE. The [API](https://ml-explore.github.io/mlx/build/html/python/_autosummary/mlx.core.fast.rope.html) accepts one offset per batch element. [Dispatch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/rope.cpp) confirms that vector offsets select a different entrypoint. Both [rotary implementations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx/v0.32.3/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/rope.metal) use matching frequency, rotation, and conversion expressions. With sequence length one and nonnegative int32 offsets C+i, their position arguments coincide. This supports an arithmetic-equivalence hypothesis, not established native bitwise parity.
proposal.generalization: Batching independent rotary operations and eliminating intermediate packing are portable reductions in invocation and copying work. They can benefit speculative verifiers that retain scalar arithmetic. The claim requires no custom kernels or compiler changes. Engines already batching RoPE gain nothing further; benefits may diminish when weight or attention traffic dominates.
proposal.risk: Different native entrypoints may still produce different bits. Head mapping, offsets, or shared-buffer handling could corrupt retained KV even when immediate predictions match. Transposed KV insertion may incur internal copies, and changed allocation lifetimes may offset savings. Native differential validation must precede activation.
proposal.history_relation: Builds directly on accepted rounds 0013, 0016, and 0017, which provide bulk KV insertion and contiguous activation blocks while retaining singleton RoPE. Round 0001’s full-transformer parity failure did not isolate rotary grouping. This preserves accepted projections, attention, drafting, and pipelining; prior weight-packing and drafting-policy results do not resolve this mechanism.

review.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Add a separate rotary eligibility gate, evaluated before cache mutation. Require the existing eligible grouped verifier, m=3 through 17, drained outputs, common cache offset C, existing capacity at least C+m, BF16 tensors, and the fixed target’s native nn.RoPE parameters: dims=64, traditional=False, base=100000, scale=1.0. Require 0 <= C and C+m-1 <= INT32_MAX. Unsupported rotary cases retain the current rotary path without disabling accepted projection grouping.

2. During decode, construct one int32 vector containing C through C+m-1 and reuse it across all layers. Build it without floating-point position arithmetic or an overflowing exclusive endpoint, for example int32 arange(m) plus int32 C. Preserve the existing Q→K→V projection dependencies and gate the rotary inputs on completion of the V block.

3. Reshape contiguous Q and K blocks to [m,9,1,64] and [m,3,1,64]. Call the original attn.rope once on each with the shared offset vector. Split rotated Q along batch into contiguous [1,9,1,64] views; do not use the existing position-axis _rows helper on this layout. Transpose rotated K with axes (2,1,0,3) to [1,3,m,64]. Reshape V to [m,3,1,64] and apply the same transpose. Pass both KV views directly to the existing bulk update. Create per-position projection trace views only when tracing is requested.

4. Preserve functional array ownership and allocated-cache layout. Keep sequential singleton attention against the original allocated-buffer prefixes ending at C+i+1, including the existing exact-capacity branch. Each attention continues to depend on both updated buffers and the preceding attention result. Preserve all subsequent operations, dtypes, and rounding boundaries. Do not manually recycle shared projection or rotary buffers.

5. Materialize every prediction before acceptance or rollback. For m-1 drafts and a accepted drafts, retain the existing emission rule and trim m-1-a entries, leaving offset C+1+a with the final emitted token pending. Preserve scalar pipelining, output budgets, prefill, shared model objects, and request isolation. Charge eligibility, offsets, views, rotary work, transfers, counters, and cleanup to decode. Add inexpensive request-local counters for active rotary blocks and actual grouped rotary calls.

6. Extend candidate/checks.py with native bitwise rotary comparisons for every m, both head counts, every row, and varied offsets, including float32 integer-precision boundaries and the permitted int32 endpoint. Use independent finite inputs covering cancellation, small and large magnitudes, signed zero, and BF16 rounding boundaries. Compare rotated tensors, complete downstream logits, and valid KV prefixes against both the current accepted verifier and actual singleton reference calls. Disable only rotary grouping for the accepted-verifier comparison. Keep the scalar oracle independent, preserve per-position trace formats, and assert trace-list lengths before comparisons so zip cannot silently omit positions.

7. Test traced and untraced execution, every acceptance length, stale-tail overwrite, exact-capacity endings, subsequent scalar growth, consecutive speculative blocks, scalar transitions, small output budgets, fallback, and fresh requests. Hooks must confirm exactly two grouped rotary calls per layer, correct vector offsets, and continued projection grouping when rotary grouping is disabled. Resolve the first numerical discrepancy before activation; matching sampled argmax tokens alone is insufficient. If native execution is unavailable, provide runnable checks and report validation as pending.

8. Freeze the implementation independently of benchmark prompts and results. Have the orchestrator perform native validation, unchanged exact-token evaluation, and both throughput confirmations against the current accepted candidate. Confirm that the new path actually executes. Retain only exact output and an incremental gain of at least 1.03x in both confirmations; record numerical validation, activation, and performance separately.
review.reason: No fundamental flaw was found. Independent in-memory checks passed 57,600 pair-address checks and 240 cache configurations, including 2,400 rollback paths and 16,640 scalar continuations. These establish indexing and cache bookkeeping only. Native BF16 parity remains pending because MLX could not access a Metal device. The review sharpens eligibility, dependencies, fallback isolation, and differential testing. Performance remains for benchmarking. No files were edited.

implementation.summary: Implemented grouped singleton RoPE with a separate eligibility gate, shared int32 offsets, direct KV views, and request-local counters. Extended native bitwise and transition checks. Syntax and diff checks pass. Native numerical validation remains pending because MLX cannot access a Metal device; correctness evaluation and benchmarking remain with the orchestrator.
